newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Coca-Cola investing billion rand in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola investing billion rand in S.Africa.

text.p: U.S. soft drinks giant Coca-Cola Co said on Monday it was joining with its seven South African bottlers to invest over one billion rand ($220 million) in the South African marketplace.

"We believe South Africa offers tremendous growth opportunities to those who show long-term discipline, and we believe the time to invest in South Africa is right now," said company president and chief operating office Doug Ivester.
Coca-Cola aims to double its business in South Africa over the next five to seven years, he said. Sales are currently running at around 4.8 billion rand a year at the retail level.
In addition to Coca-Cola, the company markets Sprite, Fanta, Sparletta, Stoney and other soft drink brands throughout South Africa, and the country is the company's 10th largest market worldwide.
Its drinks are bottled by seven South African-owned concerns -- Amalgamated Beverage Industries, Coca-Cola Bottlers Mpumalanga, Coca-Cola SABCO, Cooks, Kilimanjaro, Peninsula Beverages and Suncrush.
Competition is hotting up in the South African marketplace following Pepsico Inc's re-entry into South Africa two years ago, opening up a new front in the global cola wars.
Black townships were an early target for Pepsi but the company is now targeting all sections of the South African market.
Coke is determined to fight back. "South Africa is sacred ground to the Coca-Cola Company," said Ivester.
